title: The Demi-Human Tavern
text: “Ah, you’re back.”
After buying Filolial-sama, I met up with my Father and the others.
“How did it go? Did you get a good one?”
“There’s no such thing as ‘good’ or ‘bad’ when it comes to Filolial-sama.”
I showed my Father Filolial-sama’s egg. There’s no difference between the eggs. I wonder what kind of creature will hatch. I can’t wait to find out!
“Huh… So that bird-like monster is going to hatch from this?”
“That’s right.”
“You bought three of them? Well, if you want to move quickly, it can’t hurt… but it’ll take time, won’t it?”
“They are eggs, after all…”
“They’ll grow up in no time!”

It seems Éclair has some kind of misunderstanding about Filolial-sama! It’s true that raising them without a level boost takes time, but leave it to Motoyasu—I’ll train them into irreplaceable combatants in just a few days. In three days, they’ll likely even be able to understand human speech.
“How long will it take?”
“As a mount? I’ve heard it takes at least two weeks for a skilled warrior to raise one.”
“Two days after hatching is plenty!”
“No… that’s definitely too fast… Does the Hero possess such an ability?”

I nodded in response to Éclair’s question. That’s right—not just Filolial-sama… but all monsters in this world grow at a remarkable rate when their levels rise rapidly. This has already been proven on the estate that my Father used to manage. I’m talking about the monster stable entrusted to the pig that rode on the back of that hateful dragon who had been hostile toward Filo-tan. Even though they were pigs, they were quite well-trained monsters.
“Won’t that become clear eventually? After all, Motoyasu-kun bought them.”
“I’d really like you to take a look.”
“U-um, well then, let’s head into town and take a break.”

And so, I headed to the nearest town with my Father and the others. The town we stopped at was of moderate size—it felt like a merchant town with a strong focus on trade. It’s a neighboring country of Melromarc… I haven’t been here very often, but I believe it’s a region—if you head north—where there’s been talk of a famine. The envoy from Siltvelt led us to a tavern tucked away in a back alley. A sign reading “Demi-Human Tavern” hung outside.
“A Demi-Human tavern, huh… Indeed, it’s the perfect place to hide Lord Iwatani, the Shield Hero.”
“Yes. We’d be grateful if you could please relax in the room at the back of the tavern.”
“Is this where we get off?”
My father stepped down from the carriage and stretched. He’d been riding the whole time, after all. It’s no wonder he’s tired.
“Ah… I don’t usually get motion sickness, but it was cramped in there.”
It wasn’t one of those carriages that Filo-tan would pull—it was simply a standard carriage meant for transportation. It must have been tight.
“This way, please.”
The envoy from Siltvelt had entered the tavern and was speaking with the innkeeper.
“We’ve settled things. Please make yourselves at home.”

The innkeeper opened the door leading to the back of the tavern and stepped aside to let us pass. I’ll go through ahead of my Father to check the hallway, confirm it’s safe, and then give him the signal.
“I know, but we have to stay on our guard, don’t we?”
“That’s right. In this world, you never know when or by whom you might be devoured.”
“Well… maybe every world is much the same.”

Accompanied by the envoy from Siltvelt, we’ll take a break in the room we were shown inside the tavern. The tavern is on the first floor of a three-story stone building… We’re currently in a room on the third floor. What’s more, there’s a switch in the stone wall that leads to a secret room. Apparently, there are facilities like this all over the place. That’s probably because we’re near Melromarc, which used to be an enemy nation.
Because of this, my Father has been warned not to stand by the window for safety reasons. Sitting on the bed, he looks incredibly bored.
“It’s not as cramped as a carriage, but in the end, it’s still just hiding, isn’t it?”
“That’s true… If there’s anything you want, I, Motoyasu, will go buy it for you.”
“Hmm… We’re getting food, so if I had to pick something, I guess I’d like to take a bath…”
“Do households in this town have baths?”
“No, but we can bring hot water in a barrel as a makeshift solution.”
“Like a drum-can bath? That’d be fine.”
“A bath, you say? What about your security, Father?”
“Hm? I was planning to keep watch myself.”
“Wait, Éclair, you’re going to watch me bathe!?”
My Father blushed. Sensing his intention, Éclair also began to panic.
“N-no, that’s not it, Lord Iwatani! I’m only watching for security purposes—I’m definitely not some kind of pervert!”
“Hahaha, Éclair, how about you go to the town bathhouse while your Father is bathing? In the meantime, I, Motoyasu, will guard your Father.”
“Hmm… With Lord Kitamura’s abilities, I can rest easy. I’ll take you up on that offer. But if something were to happen to me and I never made it back, don’t go looking for me, okay?”
“Don’t worry. My companions will protect Seaetto.”
The pig accompanying the envoy from Siltvelt stepped forward and spoke to Éclair.
“That’s right. Well then, while Lord Iwatani is taking his bath, let’s go wash up ourselves.”
“U-uh-huh.”
Father looks away from Éclair, seemingly at a loss for where to look.
“Lord Iwatani… it seems you’ve misunderstood something, but I’m not really…”
What on earth are they talking about?
“That’s true, but… sorry. I ended up thinking about something I really shouldn’t have.”
“Hmm. Just think of me as a casual friend.”
“Yeah. You’re an important friend, after all. As for that sort of thing… let’s think about it once we’re safe.”

Oh? The pig with Éclair looks a bit embarrassed, too. Then Éclair and the others left the room, and it grew a little quieter inside. The envoy from Siltvelt has also stepped away to ask for hot water.
“Ah, sorry. Motoyasu-kun, it’s not like that at all! I’m just making it clear just in case. Because, well…”
My father begins to explain. What happened?

“Ms. Eclair and the others… aren’t they just treating me specially because I’m the Shield Hero? So when it comes to romance or a harem… I don’t want to do that yet. I want to be with someone who truly understands me and still wants to be friends with me anyway…”

Hmm? His reaction seems different from the Father I know. I’m pretty sure he used to hate women. There was even a “ban on romance” in that village, wasn’t there? As I watched him in silence, my Father started talking about various things. Apparently, those pigs brought by the envoy from Siltvelt had been feeding him all sorts of stories.
“They told me that if I go to Siltvelt, there’d be all sorts of marriage prospects, or that I could marry a beautiful wife…”
“That sounds dangerous.”
“Yeah. The princess of Melromarc was incredibly beautiful, too, but I have to assume there’s something fishy going on.”
“That’s just like Father. The Crimson Swine is a top priority—we must be on high alert. We should also be wary of pigs from other countries who try to flirt with us.”
“I’ve never had a girlfriend before, so I was starting to get a little carried away, but I’ll have to be careful.”
Just as I expected from Father. I, Motoyasu, am truly impressed by his ability to learn so quickly.
“According to Motoyasu-kun, this world is quite dangerous… and Siltvelt might not be any different in that regard…”
“That’s true.”

As far as I can recall, I’ve never been to Siltvelt, but in this other world, I have to be on guard against all sorts of things. Come to think of it… I seem to remember Father mentioning this before. He said he didn’t trust Siltvelt all that much because, one way or another, they’ve been trying every trick in the book to recruit the Shield Hero. Um… I think it was when my Father realized I only took slaves as subordinates that they arranged for the daughter of a Siltvelt noble to be sent to him as a slave… wasn’t it? I do remember that.

And this is exactly the kind of situation I’ve been wary of. Thinking back to before I came to this other world, I used to be quite conceited about my good looks, and I even had moments when I wondered if women were somehow seeking out my genes.

Since ancient times, physical appearance has been a key factor in how women are valued. If you’re good-looking, you’re popular. In other words, they hope to have a physical relationship and give birth to good-looking children. I’d kept that mindset in the back of my mind. Being good-looking is a good thing. But women who approach you solely for your looks are pigs. Similarly, there are plenty of pigs who approach you just for your background.

That was something I, Motoyasu, finally learned after coming to this other world. Back when I was deluded into thinking I was a huge hit just because of my reputation as the “Spear Hero”—looking back now, I want to beat that version of myself to death. After the Spirit Tortoise incident… just how cold the world became, and how I was betrayed by my own comrades. I’ll never forget the emotions I felt back then.

And it was Filo-tan who gave me a stern talking-to when I was getting too full of myself. It was the angelic Filo-tan who cheered me up when I was depressed after realizing just how cruel the world really is. Ah… that was the moment I became convinced that as long as I had Filo-tan’s love, I could go on living. Yes, life isn’t all hardship, you know.

“That’s right. Father, you mustn’t entrust your body to anyone unless you’re certain they’re an irreplaceable, beloved person. And above all, you mustn’t use the word ‘love’ when you’re not certain you can make someone happy.”

“Entrust my body…? I’m a guy, though… Yeah. I get what you mean. I’ll have to be careful. It seems people try to take advantage of me just because I’m a hero… And even though the kingdom of Siltvelt is on our side, I’ve got to make sure I don’t get used.”
As expected of my Father—he really took my words to heart and gave them some serious thought.
